title: Reproducing O'Sullivan et al. 2001: dangling bonds exposed by rapid thermal processing

sample.paper: “150 mm boron (B) doped silicon (100) wafers with a dopant concentration of approximately 1x10^15 cm-3”
sample.ours: FAMILY: Si_Planar; ORIENTATION: Si100; DOPING: p_type_boron_1e15 (recorded; no program reads it)

sample.paper: “100 mm phosphorus (P) doped silicon (100) wafers with a doping concentration of approximately 1x10^15 cm-3”
200 mm p-type Si(100), 5×10^14 cm-3 (process 3); boron 8×10^14 cm-3 (processes 4, 5)
POCl3-doped polysilicon, 3000 Å (process 1) or 4500 Å (process 2); a mercury probe for the RTO samples
sample.ours: GATE: n_poly_POCl3 | mercury_probe (recorded; no program reads it)
sample.note: No program knows that a gate exists, or that a gate or its deposition supplies hydrogen.
The vocabulary has an HF step only inside a named clean (peroxide_HF); a bare HF dip has no value, so not_stated is written.

sample.ours: the thin-oxide program's thickness; oxidation times chosen to give it
sample.note: The times are ours, so the furnace thicknesses are not a test.

history.paper: “a 120 Å oxide was grown in dry oxygen at 850 °C”
history.ours: RUN Oxidation850 DURATION 4400 TEMP 850->850 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: The time is not stated. 4400 s is ours: the time the thin-oxide program needs for 12 nm at 850 °C.

history.paper: “followed by a 60 min anneal in N2 at 850 °C”
history.ours: RUN Anneal850 DURATION 3600 TEMP 850->850 AMBIENT inert_N2

history.paper: “The ramp down rate following oxidation is 3 °C/min”
history.ours: RUN RampDown DURATION 5000 TEMP 850->600 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: The rate is stated; the gas during the ramp is not (nitrogen is ours, continuing the anneal).

history.item: Pull from the furnace at 600 °C, 8 cm/min
history.paper: “with a pull from the furnace at 600 °C at 8 cm/min”
history.ours: RUN Pull600 DURATION 600 TEMP 600->200 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: The pull speed is stated, the boat travel and so the time is not; 10 min to 200 °C in nitrogen is ours. The paper argues this slow pull is where ambient moisture re-passivates the dangling bonds; the language cannot state moisture in a pull it does not know.

history.paper: “The gate was formed by chemical vapor deposition of 3000 Å of polysilicon.”
history.note: Temperature and time not stated for process 1. The deposition is from silane, a hydrogen source the language cannot state.

history.item: Backside strip; phosphorus doping of the polysilicon from POCl3
history.paper: “the polysilicon was phosphorus doped from a POCl3 source”
history.note: Temperature and time not stated; typically 900 °C or more for tens of minutes.

history.item: Dry etch of the polysilicon; resist strip
history.paper: “Dry etching of the polysilicon layer formed capacitors of various areas.”
“Following the resist strip, the samples received a 30 min anneal in nitrogen at 900 °C.”
history.ours: RUN Anneal900 DURATION 1800 TEMP 900->900 AMBIENT inert_N2
RUN Pull900 DURATION 600 TEMP 900->200 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: Ours: 10 min to 200 °C in nitrogen, like the first withdrawal.

history.item: 1 MHz HFCV and quasi-static CV at room temperature; no forming gas
history.paper: “Neither sample received a final forming gas alloy.” (Fig. 1 caption); DOS from QSCV with the Berglund integral

history.item: Hydrogen during the polysilicon deposition and POCl3 doping
history.paper: deposition at 620 °C (process 2); POCl3 doping (both); the paper: “hydrogen passivation will inevitably occur during full device fabrication, in processes such as polysilicon deposition”
history.ours: EVENT Poly KIND deposition; EVENT POCl3 KIND deposition
history.note: The language has no silane or POCl3 and no way to say that a deposition exposes the interface to hydrogen.

history.paper: “This period, which could be hours in duration, allows hydrogen passivation from moisture in the ambient.”
history.ours: the pulls are written in dry nitrogen
history.note: The moisture of a furnace's cooling ambient is never stated; it could be written as mix:N2=…,H2O=… but its value is unknown and the trap-density program does not read water.
Without a hydrogen anneal the predictor gives midgap only; with one, the shape of one Vitkavage curve, which has no peak at 0.85 eV.
